prompt:
A 59-year-old woman with well-controlled polycythemia vera on ropeginterferon had a chest CT three months ago that showed a single large ground-glass nodule in the right lower lobe. A follow-up CT this week shows resolution of that nodule but now demonstrates new mucous plugging with peribronchial opacities and centrilobular nodules in the right middle lobe and lingula. She also takes escitalopram 10 mg daily for mild anxiety. She reports only mild recent upper-respiratory symptoms (COVID negative), with no chronic cough or dyspnea, and has no bronchiectasis or other structural lung disease. What further testing or follow-up imaging do you recommend?

Provide a comprehensive management plan including appropriate diagnostic workup, referrals, procedures if indicated, follow-up, and actions to avoid.

rubric_items.text: Arrange short-interval repeat chest CT, for example in 6–12 weeks or approximately 3 months, to assess resolution or persistence of the airway-centered abnormalities.
Review the current and prior chest CT images with thoracic radiology.
Obtain a focused history for pulmonary infection, aspiration risk, and relevant environmental exposures.
Assess current respiratory status with a focused pulmonary examination and pulse oximetry.
Provide return precautions for fever, hemoptysis, worsening cough, or dyspnea.
Arrange clinical follow-up during the short-interval surveillance period, with earlier assessment for new or worsening symptoms.
Arrange pulmonary clinic follow-up after the repeat chest CT.
Order a CBC with differential.
Obtain expectorated sputum for Gram stain and bacterial culture if a productive cough develops.

If the abnormalities persist and NTM remains a concern, obtain at least three sputum specimens for AFB smear and mycobacterial culture over an interval of at least one week, using induced sputum if necessary.
Recommend conservative mucus-clearance measures such as hydration and airway-clearance techniques.
Defer empiric antibiotics in the absence of clinical evidence of bacterial infection.
Defer bronchoscopy unless respiratory status worsens or CT abnormalities persist.
Counsel the patient to report new respiratory symptoms because ropeginterferon-associated pneumonitis is possible.
Consult hematology if concern for ropeginterferon pulmonary toxicity increases.
Obtain spirometry and DLCO if respiratory symptoms or imaging abnormalities persist.
Initiate empiric four-drug RIPE therapy for tuberculosis.
Start empiric broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics.
Start empiric broad-spectrum oral antibiotics despite the absence of bacterial infection signs.
Initiate empiric high-dose systemic corticosteroids.
Initiate empiric antifungal therapy with voriconazole or fluconazole.
Start empiric multidrug therapy for suspected nontuberculous mycobacterial infection without microbiologic confirmation.
Initiate chronic macrolide prophylaxis.
Perform CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy.
Refer for surgical or VATS lung biopsy.
Perform bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy at this stage.
Recommend tuberculosis isolation or public-health reporting without evidence of active tuberculosis.
Refer to medical oncology for metastatic malignancy evaluation based on these transient airway-centered findings.
Initiate prophylactic anticoagulation for polycythemia vera solely because of the pulmonary CT findings.
Recommend permanent cessation of ropeginterferon solely because of the nonspecific CT findings, rather than a clinically indicated temporary hold with prompt hematology coordination.
Discontinue escitalopram because of the pulmonary CT findings.
Advise that no further chest imaging or clinical follow-up is needed.
Delay repeat chest CT for 12 months without interim assessment.
Schedule monthly surveillance chest CT scans.
Order PET-CT for the resolved ground-glass nodule and new airway-centered opacities.
Order a broad autoimmune or vasculitis serology panel without supportive clinical features.
Perform immediate bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage despite mild symptoms and planned short-interval imaging.
Order broad fungal or ABPA serologic testing without compatible clinical features or bronchiectasis.
Order CT pulmonary angiography without symptoms or signs suggesting pulmonary embolism.
